content.text:
This is the as-found single-line diagram of a building's 480 V switchgear. Breakers 52-M2 and CB-03 both trip at the same moment. Nothing else changes: no other breaker opens or closes, normally-open (N.O.) breakers stay open, and Standby generator G1 is not running and does not start. A load has power only if a path of closed breakers connects it to a running source. Which loads that were running before the event have no power afterwards? A load behind an open breaker was not running. Answer with the load tags (for example CH-2), in the order they appear on the drawing from left to right, separated by commas.

Think step by step. Then end your reply with one final line in exactly this form:
FINAL ANSWER: <your answer>

message.content:
52-M2 disconnects BUS 2 and, through the closed 52-ET, BUS E. The normally-open ties remain open, while CB-04 keeps BUS 2B supplied from BUS 1 and CB-02 keeps BUS EB supplied. CB-03 also opens, disconnecting UPS-1.

FINAL ANSWER: UPS-1, CH-1, SF-2
